All three agree exactly on route, length, diameter, ownership split and commodity -- this is a real, correctly-classified interstate-scale gas transmission trunk (not gathering/feeder), explicitly called an INTRASTATE system by its own operator, so its total absence from FERC dockets is expected, not an existence concern (Texas RRC/PHMSA jurisdiction, per the scope guidance). validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 2019 to 2018 (StartMonth1=5/May) -- three independent, mutually-agreeing sources date the in-service restart to May 2018, none support 2019.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2019 does not hold up. Oil & Gas Journal (2018-05-04) reports the JV 'plan to bring the Old Ocean natural gas pipeline back into service in this year's second quarter' (i.e. Q2 2018) -- a contemporaneous announcement, not a retrospective. Natural Gas Intelligence (2022-07-07) independently states Old Ocean was 'shuttered from 2012 to 2018, was reopened under a 50/50 joint venture' -- i.e. reopened in 2018, written four years later with no stake in the original announcement. Energy Transfer Operating, L.P.'s own FY2018 Form 10-K is explicit and dated: 'In May 2018, ETO and Enterprise Products Partners L.P. announced the formation of a joint venture to resume service on the Old Ocean natural gas pipeline. The 24-inch diameter pipeline resumed service in May 2018 and ETO is the operator.' All three independently converge on May 2018, and none mentions 2019 in connection with this pipeline's start of service. This is a >=2-independent-source material date conflict (trade press announcement + trade press retrospective + operator's own dated SEC filing), not a rounding/estimate variance -- recommend Update correct the cell rather than leaving 2019 in place.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=160.00 MMcf/d is off by 25% against two independently-sourced, mutually-agreeing figures. Natural Gas Intelligence (2022-07-07) states Energy Transfer 'shut in a 0.2 Bcf/d capacity, 24-inch diameter natural gas transmission line' -- i.e. 200 MMcf/d. Energy Transfer Operating, L.P.'s FY2018 Form 10-K carries Old Ocean Pipeline, LLC in its intrastate-assets capacity table at exactly '0.2' (Bcf/d) alongside its 240-mile length and 50% ownership interest -- the same figure, from a different origin (the operator's own regulatory filing, filed in early 2019 for FY2018) four years before the NGI figure. Two independent, dated, mutually-agreeing sources naming the same 0.2 Bcf/d / 200 MMcf/d figure is a material and well-supported conflict with the sheet's 160.00 -- recommend Update correct the value (note CapacityBcm/y and CapacityBOEd are formula-derived columns and should be left to recompute, not hand-edited).
